geometryPolicy: 48 CSS pixel minimum action targets; project adaptations and unsupported variants documented in README

changes.description: All 51 catalogued components now carry the code documentation the data table had: two or three recipes each in HTML with JavaScript, Vue 3 and React, a runnable example in the playground for the first recipe of every component, and the anatomy guide with the purpose of each public slot and CSS part. The i18n collector now reads the recipe fields from their own indentation and ignores the same words inside a code sample, so only page text is collected.

Every catalogued component now carries an anatomy guide, like the data table: a sentence on where its content goes, the purpose of every public slot and CSS part, the markup of each slot, and a complete example. Slots and parts share a purpose dictionary, so the documentation of one control is consistent with the others, and the detected names always lead the list: a guide can add a purpose but never hide a public seam.

The segments of `bolle-segmented-buttons` wrapped onto a second row when the container was narrower than their content, and the pill broke into a two-line blob. The track no longer wraps: the segments keep one row, the labels never break and a container too narrow scrolls the track horizontally.

`bolle-gantt` gains the seams the other surfaces already had: `GanttColumn.render` returns the markup of a cell and `barRenderer` the content of a bar, both with `contentStyles` for their rules; the slots `loading`, `error` and `empty` and the matching `loadingRenderer`, `errorRenderer` and `emptyRenderer` replace the built-in states; `groupLabel` names a group row. The chart also selects the task the reader clicks, applying `selected` and reporting it with `task-select`.

A column `bolle-gantt` does not know stayed hidden: the width preset that picks the built-in columns also switched it off. The preset now chooses among the built-in columns only, and a column the application declares keeps the visibility it asked for.

Each component now applies the change the reader makes before reporting it, instead of waiting for the application to write the state back. `bolle-pagination` moves to the requested page and size; `bolle-data-table` applies row selection, row expansion, grouping and column pin, hide, order and width; `bolle-kanban` moves the card and folds the column; `bolle-gantt` moves the task and adds the dependency. The events `page-change`, `select`, `expand`, `group`, `column-change`, `card-move`, `column-collapse`, `task-change` and `dependency-add` report the change rather than ask for it. An application that mirrors the same state keeps working, because a later assignment still wins, but the event listener is no longer required for the component to work.

`bolle-data-table` gains `columnHandler`, called with the new column list after every pin, hide, reorder or width change, for applications that store the layout outside the page: the table applies the change first and redraws again once the returned promise settles.

`bolle-data-table` sorts and pages on its own: a header click goes ascending then descending and never drops the order, `page-size` slices the rows it holds, `total` falls back to their count and the requested page is clamped to the pages the data has. The new properties `sortHandler` and `pageHandler` take over only when the application loads the data from a server: the table calls them with the requested order or page, keeps the `sort` and `page-change` events, and redraws once the returned promise settles, so an in-place change to `rows` is shown without a manual `refresh()`. A header click therefore no longer needs an application sort, and the `sort` property is the current order rather than only the incoming one.

Boolean properties that defaulted to true now default to false, as the Lit reactive-properties guide requires for an attribute-controlled boolean: `bolle-gantt` `editable` and `linkable`, `bolle-kanban` `movable`, `bolle-widget` `removable`, `movable` and `resizable`, `bolle-bottom-app-bar` `divider`, `bolle-dialog` `modal`. Markup can now turn each feature off by removing the attribute; `bolle-side-sheet` keeps `modal` on because it always blocks the page. The documentation examples set the attribute explicitly, and the redundant `attribute: false` next to `state: true` is removed from seven internal properties.

The data table documentation states the reactivity contract: the component reads the array it receives and the frameworks pass a new array on every change. An in-place mutation is invisible to the component, so Vue and React examples derive a new array with `toSorted`, and `refresh()` covers the imperative case.

`bolle-data-table` gains the public method `refresh()`, which redraws the rows after the application changed its own array in place. Assigning the same array back does not reach the component, because the property keeps its identity, so the method replaces the copy-then-assign workaround in the sorting example.

`bolle-list` gains `itemRenderer`, which the component calls for every row, replacing the per-item `leading-{id}` and `trailing-{id}` slots. The same correction removes the per-item slots of `bolle-sidebar`, `bolle-kanban` and `bolle-data-table`: the application supplies one renderer per element kind and the component calls it, so no caller prepares one slot per row.

`bolle-data-table` exposes public CSS parts and the shell slots `header`, `loading`, `error`, `empty`, `empty-state` and `footer`. Cell, row, detail and group content arrives from renderers the component calls: `column.render`, `rowRenderer`, `headerRenderer`, `detail`, `groupSummary`, `groupRenderer`, plus loading, error, empty and footer renderers. Row, header and group heights, column widths and virtual overscan are configurable; the sorting, selection, paging and column-change event contract is unchanged.

`bolle-kanban` exposes public CSS parts, configurable column width and gaps, and the state slots `loading`, `error` and `empty`. Card, column and lane content arrives from the renderers the component calls (`card`, `columnRenderer`, `laneRenderer`), so the application never pre-declares one slot per item. Card grips reach 48px and the move and action event contract is unchanged.

`bolle-dashboard` and `bolle-widget` gain configurable compact, medium and full column counts, public anatomy parts and slots, movable/resizable controls, and 48px grip and resize targets. The grid reflows at 600, 840 and 1200px and keeps the application-owned layout contract.

`bolle-app-shell` exposes configurable medium and expanded breakpoints, supporting pane mode, public CSS parts and slots for inline or modal supporting content and compact navigation. Pane, supporting, status and spacing geometry use component-token fallbacks, and dynamic slot changes update the shell regions. The documentation demo removes the narrow topbar overflow.

`bolle-sidebar` exposes public CSS parts and the slots `header`, `filter`, `empty` and `footer`. Item and rail content arrives from the `item` and `railItem` renderers the component calls, so the application never pre-declares one slot per row. Width bounds and geometry are configurable, row and resize targets reach 48px, and action-only entries render as buttons instead of links with a fragment URL.

All Material 3 components outside Schiuma expose a public anatomy contract through CSS parts and named slots. Component-token fallbacks cover the configurable geometry introduced for actions, inputs, navigation, feedback and overlays. Native form, link, picker and slider options are forwarded where the platform supports them, with accessible slot labels and required picker validation. The documentation derives properties, slots and parts from the registered implementation and publishes copyable examples.

`bolle-gantt` adds the planning surface of the Schiuma group: tasks declared by the application on a time axis with four scales, summary bars, milestones, dependencies, approved-plan baseline, workload per resource, configurable columns, virtualised rows and changes by pointer or keyboard. It never modifies a task: it asks with `task-change`, reports the refusal with `task-change-blocked` applying the rule passed in `restrict`, and reports the opening with `task-open`; a dependency that already exists or closes a loop is refused by the surface itself with `dependency-blocked`. View state — scale, density, baseline — is reported with `view-change` and the visible columns with `columns-change`.

Two Schiuma components for navigation and identity: `bolle-breadcrumb` renders the path the application declares, marks the current level with `aria-current`, shortens a long path behind an expandable gap with `max-items`, mirrors the chevron separator in a right-to-left layout and reports the chosen level with `breadcrumb-select`; `bolle-avatar-group` arranges the `bolle-avatar` children it receives in an overlapping row, keeps the first `max` visible and sums the rest, including the people declared with `total`, in an overflow bubble that becomes a button with `interactive` and emits `avatar-group-select`. `bolle-avatar` gains an optional ring of the surface colour, so an avatar stays separate from the one it overlaps.

Menus close the interaction gaps recorded in the previous audit: a built-in `filterable` field with `filter`, `locale` and an empty state, submenu dismissal when the pointer leaves item and submenu, the surface exit transition kept alive while the submenu animates out, an origin-aware ripple through a clipped layer, root `selectedIds` that aggregates nested selection and a compact form that turns the vertical menu into a bottom sheet below `compact-width`. Spring easings are now sampled from the spring tokens by `npm run motion` and used by the floating surfaces, `npm run colors` writes medium and high contrast presets as `data-contrast` blocks, the loading indicator gains a seven-shape `morph` variant, carousel keylines follow the component width through container query units, and the documentation overview prints a state matrix derived from the component definitions.

Four common components that were missing: `bolle-bottom-app-bar` closes the Material 3 catalogue with a bottom container for actions, an end slot and an optional docked FAB, in a standard or floating form; `bolle-avatar`, `bolle-empty-state` and `bolle-pagination` are Schiuma primitives that the library itself was duplicating. The data table now renders `bolle-pagination` for its pager and `bolle-empty-state` for the empty and error rows, the kanban renders the same state for loading, error and empty, and the documentation demos drop their hand-written initials circle in favour of `bolle-avatar`. Component tokens `--md-comp-bottom-app-bar-*` and `--md-comp-avatar-*-size` added; pagination labels in English, Italian, French and Simplified Chinese.

`bolle-dashboard` takes the drag interaction promoted with `bolle-kanban`: dragging a tile by its handle now carries a copy that follows the pointer, opens a dashed gap in the slot the tile will occupy, names the position in the pointer note, refuses a drop outside the dashboard and scrolls the page or the nearest scroll container at the edges; Escape cancels with an announcement. Tile hover becomes a state layer on the surface, because the lift belongs to the moving copy, and Alt+arrows and the tile menu keep working as the path without dragging.

New Schiuma component `bolle-kanban` promoted from the approved prototype. The board renders columns and cards the application owns, moves them by pointer drag with a copy that follows the pointer, a dashed placeholder, a refused column in the error role and edge autoscroll, or by Alt+arrows from the card handle, and asks with `card-move` while `restrict` returns the reason a move is refused. Columns report the advised `wip` overrun without blocking, fold with `collapsed`, and carry the vertical scrolling so the board itself does not scroll; `lanes` stacks the cards in strips and `addable` offers a quick add. Card and column menus come from `cardActions` and `columnActions`, and the loading, error and empty states follow the table and shell contract.

New Schiuma components `bolle-app-shell` and `bolle-dashboard` with `bolle-widget`, promoted from the approved prototype. The shell lays out the bar, navigation, content, supporting pane, status and bottom bar as slots and picks the form from its own width, with `form` to force one and `form-change` to report it. The dashboard arranges twelve-column tiles that declare `span` and `min-span`, reorder them by drag, Alt+arrows or menu and resize them by handle, arrows or menu, reporting every change in `layout-change` and `widget-hide` while keeping the layout with the application.

Documentation site: App shell and Dashboard pages in the Schiuma section, with an interactive application preview that adapts to the stage width, a standalone dashboard preview that prints the layout it reports, controls for form, density, columns and supporting pane, and generated HTML, Vue and React snippets.

New Schiuma component `bolle-data-table`: a controlled table whose application owns rows, sorting, paging, grouping and selection and answers them through events. Columns carry width, alignment, pinning, grouping and a renderer; sorting keeps ranks and `aria-sort`; the header menu covers sorting, grouping, pinning, moving and hiding; columns drag with Escape and Alt+arrows; the resize handle works by pointer, double click and arrows. Selection, row details, group summaries, a pager, windowed rendering, loading/updating/empty/error states, `card` and `free` forms and two densities. Markup returned by renderers is styled through `contentStyles`.

Documentation site: Data table page in the Schiuma section with an interactive preview (sorting, grouping, paging, selection, details, column menu), controls, HTML/Vue/React snippets and the generated API table. The playground gives this entry the full width with the parameters underneath.

`bolle-menu` opens towards the wider side of the viewport on both axes: a menu under or over its anchor, a submenu beside its item, then clamps inside the viewport. Before, it opened below and in the reading direction and flipped only on overflow. Placement now reads the layout size of the surface: measuring during the entry animation read a scaled box, so the menu ran past its anchor and a submenu covered its parent.

`bolle-sidebar` gains `search`: `field` (default text field), `contained` or `divided` to filter with `bolle-search` in that appearance, `none` to hide the filter. The documentation site gives sidebar variants a column wide and tall enough to show the whole panel.

New Schiuma group for admin applications, outside the Material catalogue. First component `bolle-sidebar`: navigation tree up to three levels, filter, counters, ellipsis with a tooltip on cut labels, rail form with a menu beside it, resize grip (220–480px) and `edge`/`card` forms, built only on existing tokens.

Tail is optional: `tail="none"` on card, menu, tooltip, FAB menu and snackbar drops the narrow corner and keeps the same radius on all four corners. Documented in foundations, README and the component controls.

Token set cleanup: one declaration of `--md-sys-elevation-level2` (the second copy only repeated the value), and the two menu item shapes removed because item corners now derive from the container radius.
A link card shows one hover layer: the anchor inside the card no longer adds the shared link hover and glint on top of the card state layer.

Nested surfaces share one radius rule: an inner surface takes the container radius minus the padding the container applies, with a 2px floor. Dialogs, sheets and cards publish the value as `--bb-inset-radius` and a card placed inside them inherits it; the card tail is clamped to the card radius. Menu items, autocomplete and search suggestions derive their corners from the container radius, and docked date picker and time picker fields derive theirs from the calendar or dialog padding.

Built-in messages in French and Simplified Chinese besides English and Italian, chosen from the language subtag (`supportedLocale`); tab scroll buttons and the rich tooltip dismiss button are now localized instead of fixed English.

Tooltips wider than their trigger align their tail corner over the trigger centre (start-aligned, end-aligned near the right edge) instead of centring, and the tail side is computed from the final position rather than from the box scaled by the entry animation.
Slider `compact` attribute for the bubble variant: a 32px row with the value beside the label; the value bubble appears only while dragging or with keyboard focus.

Card `tail` property (`bottom-start` default, `bottom-end`, `top-start`, `top-end`) so the narrow corner points at where the card comes from. Link cards (`href`) make the whole surface the target, with a hover state layer, a raised float on elevated cards and a focus ring.

Scrollbars inside components have no arrow buttons and round track and thumb ends, inset from the container edges (`--bb-scrollbar-*`). Tabs with a fixed height keep the tab row in place and scroll only the panel.
List rows render the trailing count badge declared by the item `badge`, on the top-level rows and on the nested ones, with the badge tokens already used by tabs and the drawer.

Search bar geometry: the field wrapper grows with the bar, the input fills it, the label and supporting text stay only in the accessibility tree and the focus indicator is drawn on the bar instead of a smaller box inside it.
Connected button group inner corners follow the M3 per-size values (XS 4dp, S/M 8dp, L 16dp, XL 20dp) with the hovered growth specified for each size, instead of reusing the shape scale.
Select and autocomplete components over native options; per-component spacing tokens with Material names for navigation rail, list, carousel and search bar; field height and vertical padding tokens.
35 component entries, public types, shared action/form/surface tokens and catalogue examples; existing menu and generated typography retained.
